set.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal funds: HOME projects with 12 or more assisted units trigger Davis-Bacon under 24 CFR 92.354; CDBG-assisted residential projects with 8 or more units trigger Davis-Bacon under Section 110 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974. PLHA alone does not set a federal wage rule.

set.affordability_requirement: No fixed percentage. Housing Element Policy H.1.5 and Action H.1.5.1 require an Affordable Housing Plan approved at the earliest entitlement (Specific Plan, Development Agreement or other primary entitlement) projecting units by extremely low, very low, low and moderate income and the ownership and rental split, set case by case by City Council.
set.layering_notes: For affordable developers the practical effect is land: master plan developers (Rio del Oro, Suncreek, Arboretum, Westborough, etc.) often satisfy the plan by dedicating sites or paying per-door in-lieu fees, which creates site opportunities and sometimes developer contributions for 9% and 4% deals. Per Action H.1.5.1, contributed land may be used by the City and its nonprofit partners, and the City will pursue supplemental funding to reach below 50% AMI. Sources: May 6, 2026 Keyser Marston memo for Sacramento County, and the HCD-hosted 2021-2029 Housing Element draft (March 24, 2021); the City site itself blocks automated access.

reason: County memo and HCD-hosted Housing Element both confirm the Affordable Housing Plan requirement and compliance options; affordability text tightened to the policy language.

set.typical_award_size: Fee source, not a subsidy program with published terms. Rates were raised in June 2022 to the regional average after no update since 1992. Revenue goes to the City Housing Trust Fund administered by the Housing and Grants Division; fund balance and any lending terms not published.
